title: Bakewell Tart
subtitle: shortcrust pastry with jam and almond frangipane
excerpt: A Bakewell tart has three layers: crisp pastry, a thin coat of raspberry jam, and a dense almond frangipane filling. It is not the iced version sold in shops -- this is the original, simpler tart from Derbyshire.
sourceNotes: The Bakewell tart comes from Bakewell in Derbyshire. The frangipane filling distinguishes it from a Bakewell pudding, which uses a puff pastry case and egg custard.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well. Defrost at room temperature for 2 hours.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Blind bake the case the day before. Fill and bake on the day.

content.text: The frangipane should be level with the top of the pastry case when it goes in -- it will rise slightly during baking. Do not overfill. The jam layer should be thin; it is there for flavour contrast, not to be the main event.

items.prepNote: 1 yolk for pastry, 2 whole eggs for frangipane

content.text: Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour with the 30g sugar. Add the egg yolk and 2 tablespoons of cold water. Bring together, flatten into a disc, and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll the pastry to 3mm and line a 23cm tart tin. Blind bake for 15 minutes, remove beans, bake 5 more minutes. Reduce oven to 180C.
Make the frangipane: beat the softened butter with the 100g caster sugar until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the ground almonds and vanilla extract.
Spread the raspberry jam thinly over the pastry base. Spoon the frangipane on top and smooth level.
Bake at 180C for 30 to 35 minutes until the frangipane is golden and set -- it should not wobble in the centre. Cool in the tin before slicing.

items.symptom: Frangipane is sunken in the middle
items.cause: Under-baked, or oven door opened too early.
items.fix: Wait until the tart is fully set before opening the oven. A skewer should come out clean.

items.symptom: Pastry is soggy under the jam
items.cause: Pastry was not blind baked long enough.
items.fix: Make sure the base is dry and pale golden before adding the filling. 20 minutes of blind baking is correct.

content.text: Bakewell is a market town in the Peak District, and both the tart and the older Bakewell pudding are claimed as local specialities. The tart version -- with frangipane instead of egg custard -- is now the version most people recognise. It appears in cake shops, bakeries, and home kitchens across Britain and is a tea-time classic.
